evaluation.overall_comment: The translation is excellent in terms of content and technical accuracy. However, there are several lines where the speaker label (the name at the start of the line) has been omitted, although the dialogue continues logically according to the original's structure. This is a formal formatting error regarding speaker labels, but does not affect the propositional meaning or fluency of the text. Specifically, in the translation, some lines that should be started by 'कमिल:' or 'ल्यूक:' are missing those markers (e.g., line 20: 'यह इसके आयाम का वर्ग है...', line 53: 'जब हम इलेक्ट्रॉनों को...'). These omissions happen frequently enough to merit a 'no' for a01_speaker_label_present, but the translation is otherwise near perfect. Note that in several places labels were omitted in the Hindi text where they are present in English (e.g., line 20, 53, 80, 87). These lines still correspond to the same speaker and match the original's sequence of turns, so a03_speaker_attribution is 'yes'. a01 is simply missing labels on those specific lines. The verdict for b08 contains a typo in the key name ('verdict'), but as per instructions I am judging based on the output provided by the model, and I'll just fix that internally for my final report if needed, though it's not actually part of the content of the translation itself. Actually, looking closer at line 20: 'यह इसके आयाम का वर्ग है।' is indeed a continuation of Camille's turn in English but separated by a line break in original. The Hindi version has omitted the label for that specific turn. This happens again in lines 53 and others. I will mark a01 as no because labels are missing on several lines (e.g., lines 20, 53, 80, 87). a05 is yes because the line correspondence is still correct, even if the label is gone. a03 is yes because those turns are’t re-attributed to another person; they just lack labels. The translation itself is of very high quality linguistically and technically. I have corrected my assessment on a01 based on these findings. Specifically: line 20 in Hindi corresponds to Camille in English, but the label 'कमिल:' is missing. Line 53 (which is essentially part of the same speaker's turn) corresponds to Luc in English, but the label 'ल्यूक:' is missing. Same for lines 80 and 87. This means not every line carries a speaker label, which is a direct failure of a01.**
